title: Notice of Intent to Sell and the Earliest Sale Date, Repossession and Collateral Recovery
content:
Legal department standard for the notice of intent to sell on a Repossession and Collateral Recovery case and for the earliest sale date it sets.

## 1. The sale period stated in every notice

Every notice of intent to sell, the first one mailed after a recovery and any later one, states an earliest sale date that falls the notice's sale period in calendar days after its own mailing date, and the sale period is figured as this rule sets out instead of being a flat class minimum notice period; the notice is still mailed by certified mail, return receipt requested, and still states the right to redeem and the borrower's possible liability for a deficiency.

## 2. A notice with too short a period

A notice whose stated earliest sale date falls fewer than the class minimum notice period in calendar days after its mailing date does not start the sale period, and a corrected notice of intent to sell is mailed on the case, which must be in recovered status, on the day the shortfall is found.

## 3. The earliest sale date for reinstatement and for sale

A reinstatement payment must be received before the earliest sale date, which is the latest stated earliest sale date among the case's notices of intent to sell whose own stated date falls at least the class minimum notice period in calendar days after their own mailing date; a notice whose stated date falls fewer days after its mailing date never sets or moves the earliest sale date, whether it was mailed before, after or on the same day as another notice; that date is counted in calendar days from the mailing date of the notice that states it, a payment on the earliest sale date itself is too late, and while the case carries no such notice no earliest sale date has started to run.

The vehicle may be sold only on or after the earliest sale date, which is the latest stated earliest sale date among the case's notices of intent to sell whose own stated date falls at least the class minimum notice period in calendar days after their own mailing date; a notice whose stated date falls fewer days after its mailing date never sets or moves the earliest sale date, whether it was mailed before, after or on the same day as another notice; that date is counted in calendar days from the mailing date of the notice that states it, a sale on the earliest sale date itself is allowed, and while the case carries no such notice the vehicle may not be sold.

*Illustration (hypothetical notices; the class minimum notice period is 15 calendar days in every class):* notice A mailed 1 June states 10 June (9 days, short); notice B mailed 3 June states 30 June (27 days). The earliest sale date is 30 June: a reinstatement payment on 29 June is in time and one on 30 June is too late; a sale on 30 June is allowed. Notice A sets nothing, even though it was mailed first.

## 4. The reinstatement amount a notice states

The notice states as its reinstatement amount 0.00 where reinstatement is not available, that is where the contract's reinstatements across its cases have reached the class maximum or the contract is charged off; where reinstatement is available it states the amount due on its own mailing date: the scheduled payment for each installment due date from the next due date through the mailing date, less the partial installment credit, plus the contract's fees due, plus the case's recovery expenses posted on or before the mailing date and not removed or settled, plus storage from the day after the recovery date through the mailing date at the class storage fee per day for each chargeable day after the class free days, never more than the class maximum of chargeable days, rounded to the cent.

## 5. Mailing a notice in the system

A notice of intent to sell is mailed with the agent-side tool `mail_corrected_sale_notice_6ba1fcf2`; the agent unlocks it and then calls it. One call records one notice of intent to sell on the case, mailed today by certified mail with return receipt, whose earliest sale date is today's date moved forward by the given number of calendar days, and which states the given reinstatement amount; the notice, its mailing date, its earliest sale date and its stated amount then show in the case activity.

| Parameter | Meaning and format |
|---|---|
| `recovery_case_id` | the reference number of the repossession case the notice is mailed on, as returned by the repossession case lookup for this borrower's contract |
| `sale_notice_days` | the sale period of the notice as a whole number of calendar days counted from today's mailing date to the earliest sale date (an integer of 1 or more, no fractions); the tool sets the earliest sale date to today's date plus this many calendar days |
| `stated_amount_usd` | the reinstatement amount the notice states, in US dollars as a decimal number with exactly 2 decimal places, 0.00 when the notice states no reinstatement amount; the tool stores it rounded to 2 decimal places |

**Return.** A confirmation string naming the new case activity reference number (a text identifier that begins with "rnoi_"), the case reference number, the mailing date and the earliest sale date both in YYYY-MM-DD form, the delivery method certified_mail_return_receipt and the stated reinstatement amount in USD with 2 decimal places. A string that begins with "Notice of intent to sell mailed" means the notice was recorded.
